data.source_title: Appointment Wait Time, Primary Care Provider Status, and Patient Demographics are Associated With Nonattendance at Outpatient Gastroenterology Clinic
data.locator: PubMed abstract, Study and Results; missed appointments among scheduled adult GI visits.
data.source_setting: Adult gastroenterology clinic at Banner University Medical Center, academic setting.
data.quantity: Missed appointments among scheduled outpatient GI appointments
data.source_evidence_basis: The study abstract reports 195 missed appointments among 2,331 scheduled visits using EHR data and a case-control design.
data.limitations: Single specialty, single center, historical cohort. This is an observed clinic-specific share, not a general outpatient no-show rate or an RWJ measurement; missed appointment categories may not match other systems.
data.inferred_scenario_use: A bounded external example of a no-show endpoint for specialty scheduling models. Preserve its GI setting and denominator and do not assign it as a local probability.

data.source_title: Appointment Wait Time, Primary Care Provider Status, and Patient Demographics are Associated With Nonattendance at Outpatient Gastroenterology Clinic
data.locator: PubMed abstract, Results; adjusted association between referral-to-appointment waiting time and missed visit.
data.source_n: 2,331 total scheduled appointments; 195 missed. Regression analytic sample size and case/control sampling weights are not specified in the accessible abstract.
data.quantity: Adjusted odds ratio for missed visit associated with longer referral-to-appointment wait time (increment unit unspecified in accessible abstract)
data.unit: adjusted odds ratio; wait-time increment unit not reported in accessible abstract
data.source_evidence_basis: The abstract reports a positive adjusted association between a longer referral-to-appointment interval and missed visits; it also says patients with a PCP were less likely to miss.
data.limitations: Observational case-control association; cannot establish that reducing wait time causes fewer no-shows. Accessible abstract omits the wait-time increment unit and regression analytic n; do not interpret this as a per-day slope or numerically convert to probabilities. No baseline risk by wait-time stratum or dose-response distribution is available in the abstract.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use only as qualitative evidence that lead time may relate to attendance. Do not apply the odds ratio as a per-day sensitivity or convert it into a local event probability; first inspect the full methods and calibrate against local data.
